text.p: English golfer David Carter, who needed an emergency brain operation seven weeks ago, is itching for his return to competition on Thursday on a course where he set a record a year ago.
The South African-born Carter was close to death on the eve of the Desert Classic in Dubai late in February suffering from fluid on the brain, and it took emergency surgery to help him recover.
The 24-year-old resident of Chesterfield spent last Sunday watching his soccer team in their nailbiting 3-3 extra-time F.A. Cup semifinal draw with Middlesbrough.
That convinced him his nerve was ready for his golfing comeback and now he is hoping to go one better than last year when the Cannes Open begins on Thursday.
He is convinced he is not starting back too soon.
"Everybody is telling me to lay off a bit longer and calm down," said Carter, holder of the course-record nine-under-par 62 for the 6,594-yard course in the south of France.
"But I'm itching to get back. I'm not too tired and I could hardly choose a better place to make my comeback than the course where I broke the record."

However, Carter confessed he remembers little of that second round last year, which almost set up victory as he finished runner-up to Scot Raymond Russell, coincidentally his partner in the opening two rounds this week.
"With most records, the round is over before you've thought about it and it wasn't until my caddie told me I needed birdie on the last for a 61 that I woke up to the fact," added Carter.

"I've been trying to remember the 62 in bed but I can't. That's hardly surprising because when I was in hospital in Dubai after the operation which saved my life, I didn't know what was going on around me.
"For a time I didn't know who I was, didn't know anything."
He had been found unconscious in his hotel bed by close friends who called in the paramedics.
Carter found Sunday's soccer match "nerve-wracking enough. But it won't be nerves I'll have for my comeback, more worry that I have to play thinking golf again."

His chief protaganist last year, Russell, said: "It's great to see him back. He's going to be the one to beat again, I'm sure, because he was playing well before his illness. He's proved he can play well here with that 62."
Russell will take his inspiration for this week from the man of the moment, Masters champion Tiger Woods.
"We've all got to practice harder now," said the Scot.
Another player making a comeback in Cannes after problems in Dubai is Europe's 1996 Rookie of the Year Thomas Bjorn, who pulled out of the Desert Classic with a recurring neck injury.
Bjorn, winner of the Loch Lomond Invitational last year, is close to Ryder Cup automatic qualification despite dropping to fourth from third place in the table last week.
For starters, Bjorn posted a 65 in Wednesday's pro-am.
